name: alert
summary: Explains contextual information, success, warnings, or failures with optional recovery navigation.

agent.useWhen: A page region needs a short explanation, consequence, or real recovery destination; choose a heading level appropriate to its document outline and an appearance that fits the surface.
agent.avoidWhen: The message is a transient toast, field validation, empty result, dismissible notice, command, or lifecycle-driven interaction.

invariants: Configuration selects one of info, success, warning, or danger tone; appearance is soft, outlined, or accent (default soft).
Heading level is h2, h3, or h4 (default h2); it changes semantic heading markup without changing the visual title style.
Title and body are required nonblank plain text and are escaped; markup, template expressions, and event attributes are never admitted from values.
The tone selects a decorative icon from the closed package catalog: info uses info, success uses check, warning and danger use alert. Text remains meaningful without color or icon.
recoveryLabel and recoveryHref must be supplied together and render as one real navigation link; unsafe destinations are rejected. No command or dismissal is created.
Announcement defaults to none; only explicit polite or assertive choices create the corresponding role and aria-live value. Announcement choice is configuration, not browser-managed lifecycle.
The section contains the selected heading, description, decorative icon, and optional recovery link in source order; the app owns any dynamic replacement lifecycle.
Recovery link placement adapts to the component container width, not the viewport. There is no browser-local state, dismissal, event output, script, or hidden follow-up behavior.
The fragment requires exactly one [[attributes]], [[icon]], [[heading]], [[body]], and [[recovery]] slot and is expanded in one pass.
